reasoning: Mandatory answer-first hook test on a reel with 4 content slides. Human body is our most consistent reach driver, and direct-claim hooks with a concrete claim ('You're shorter tonight than this morning', 109 reach, 65.5 skip) did well. Bone count, roughly 300 at birth versus 206 in adults, is a fresh, well-documented, number-led surprise that fits the hook in 8 words. The slides explain the fusion: cartilage, skull soft spots, sacrum, and where most bones end up. Palette 2 and mystery music keep the rotation going. topic: Bone fusion: babies have about 300 bones, adults 206
hook: Babies have about 300 bones. You have 206.

slides.title: Built to fuse
slides.body: Many baby bones start as separate pieces of cartilage. As you grow, they harden and fuse into fewer, bigger bones.
slides.image_prompt: Small soft cartilage pieces slowly merging into one solid white bone, on a dark background with soft studio light

slides.title: The soft spot
slides.body: A newborn's skull is several plates with gaps between them. The big soft spot on top usually closes by 18 to 24 months.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical model of a tiny infant skull with visible gaps between bone plates, museum lighting, dark backdrop

slides.title: Five become one
slides.body: Your sacrum, at the base of the spine, starts as five separate vertebrae. They fuse into a single bone by adulthood.
slides.image_prompt: Five small vertebrae lined up merging into one triangular sacrum bone, anatomical model on dark background

slides.title: Most hide in hands, feet
slides.body: Your hands and feet hold 106 of your 206 bones. That's more than half your entire skeleton.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing x-ray style skeleton of a hand and foot side by side, blue tones, dark background

cta: Follow for a new body fact every day
caption:
You were born with roughly 300 bones, and you've lost about 94 since. Nothing went missing, though. They fused together as you grew.

Your skull started as several plates with soft gaps, so you could fit through the birth canal and your brain could grow. Some bones keep fusing into your twenties.
